title: OpenAI's first phone may be built by Foxconn, the company behind iPhones
excerpt: OpenAI's phone plans just got more real
content_html:
Published Nov 19, 2026, 1:47 PM EST

Anvinraj Valiyathara is a technology journalist with more than 15 years of experience covering the global tech industry. He has published over 20,000 articles across outlets including GizmoChina, Croma Unboxed, MySmartPrice, Pricebaba, Playfuldroid, BGR India, Free Press Journal, and IBTimes.

He specializes in tech news, leaks, smartphones, consumer electronics, and emerging technologies and has reviewed everything from phones and tablets to wearables.

Anvinraj is known for accuracy and for turning complex technical developments into clear, accessible stories. Outside work, he's a Formula 1 fan who loves to travel.

OpenAI has reportedly picked the same company that assembles iPhones for its first phone. A report on Sohu, citing supply chain sources, says Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has won an order to take part in assembling the finished phones. Foxconn is already Apple’s main iPhone assembler.

Product plans, order size, and mass production arrangements are still unknown, the report says. If an OpenAI phone eventually goes on sale, the company would enter the smartphone market and could compete more directly with today’s phone brands around AI interaction.

For now, ChatGPT still lives as an app on phones other companies make. OpenAI has officially discussed hardware with former Apple design chief John Ive after the IO team merged with the company in 2025, but it has not announced a smartphone.

This isn’t the first supply chain name attached to the project

Kuo earlier pointed to a different manufacturer

On April 27, 2026, well-known analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said that OpenAI was working with MediaTek and Qualcomm on smartphone processors, with Luxshare as the exclusive system co-design and manufacturing partner. He expected mass production in 2028, and said specifications and suppliers would be finalized by late 2026 or the first quarter of 2027. Kuo argued that only by controlling both the operating system and the hardware could OpenAI deliver a full AI agent service, because a phone is the device that captures a user’s real-time state.

He updated that view on May 5, 2026, saying OpenAI appeared to be fast-tracking the project, with mass production targeted as early as the first half of 2027. MediaTek, he wrote, looked better placed to become the sole processor supplier, using a customized Dimensity 9600 built on TSMC’s N2P process. He also listed a dual-NPU design, LPDDR6 memory, UFS 5.0 storage, and an image signal processor meant to improve real-world visual sensing. If development stayed on track, Kuo estimated combined 2027 and 2028 shipments could reach around 30 million units.

The new Sohu report does not mention Luxshare, chips, or volumes, and it doesn’t call FIH Mobile the exclusive manufacturer, only a participant in assembly. In his April note, Kuo had already said Luxshare would struggle to overtake Hon Hai, Foxconn’s parent, in Apple’s assembly chain. If this report holds, that same group’s phone-making arm is now said to be lining up OpenAI’s assembly work.
